messages.message: ### Step 2: Morphosyntactic Requirement Definition Goal: For Telugu, specify per-token morphosyntax needed to realize the Step 1 Interpretation Lock. Output: ONE Markdown table only (no prose). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Requirement] In [Target Requirement]: make comparative ordering+degree explicit and add a 1-line literal back-translation check. Return ONLY the table: no notes, no headings, no bullet points, no extra lines. Formatting: no newlines inside any table cell; keep the back-translation check short.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Requirement | |-------------|-----------------------|--------------------| | Ahi | Exclamatory expression of emotion | Interjection “అయ్యో!” placed sentence‑initial, no inflection, independent clause marker. [BT: Ah!] | | quanto | Marks degree of difficulty | Degree adverb “ఎంత” modifying infinitival clause, positioned before verb, agrees with following verb phrase. [BT: how] | | a | Introduces infinitive “to” | Infinitive marker “కు” attached to verb “చెప్పు”, forming “చెప్పడానికి”. [BT: to] | | dir | Act of stating or describing | Verb root “చెప్పు” in infinitive form with “కు”, aspectually neutral. [BT: tell] | | qual | Introduces content of statement | Interrogative adjective “ఏది” modifying copular verb, placed before past verb “ఉంది”. [BT: what] | | era | Past state of the referent | Past imperfect of “ఉండు” → “ఉన్నది” with past context, agreement with neuter. [BT: was] | | è | Present state of “thing” | Present copula “అది” (or zero‑copula) linking subject to predicate. [BT: is] | | cosa | Abstract entity being described | Noun “వస్తువు” in nominative, serves as subject complement. [BT: thing] | | dura | Property of the “thing” (hard/difficult) | Adjective “కఠినమైన” agreeing in gender/number with “వస్తువు”. [BT: hard] | | esta | Points to a specific forest | Demonstrative adjective “ఈ” agreeing with feminine noun “అడవి”. [BT: this] | | selva | The physical environment (forest) | Noun “అడవి” in nominative, singular, feminine. [BT: wood/forest] | | selvaggia | Describes forest’s untamed nature | Adjective “అరణ్య” (wild) agreeing with “అడవి”. [BT: wild] | | e | Joins adjectives | Conjunction “మరియు” linking adjectives, no inflection. [BT: and] | | aspra | Describes forest’s texture (rough) | Adjective “కఠినమైన” (rough) agreeing with “అడవి”. [BT: rough] | | e | Joins adjectives | Conjunction “మరియు” linking adjectives, no inflection. [BT: and] | | forte | Describes forest’s density/strength | Adjective “బలమైన” (strong/dense) agreeing with “అడవి”. [BT: dense/strong] | | che | Refers back to selva | Relative pronoun “అది” introducing relative clause, agrees with antecedent. [BT: which] | | nel | Locates mental space | Preposition “లో” combined with noun “ఆలోచన” to form “ఆలోచనలో”. [BT: in the] | | pensier | The mental arena where effect occurs | Noun “ఆలోచన” in locative case via “లో”. [BT: thought] | | rinova | Causes fear to re‑appear | Verb “పునరుద్ధరించు” in present third‑person singular, agrees with subject “అడవి”. [BT: renews] | | la | Specifies the fear | Definite article omitted; noun “భయం” stands alone. [BT: the] | | paura | Emotional response being renewed | Noun “భయం” in accusative marked by particle “ను”. [BT: fear] |

### Step 3: Lexical Inventory & Syntactic Assembly Task: For each source line, list ALL required lexical items from Step 2, then assemble into Telugu. Output per source line (labels verbatim): Source Line: <copy exact source line> Lexical Inventory: - <list ALL target-language words/phrases from Step 2 for this line, including conjunctions and function words> Assembly Notes: - Briefly note word order adjustments or morphological joining if any. Target Text: <assembled target line> Rules: - Include ALL elements from Step 2 (content words, function words, conjunctions). Missing elements cause coverage failures. - No new content words beyond Step 2 inventory. - Punctuation: copy only end punctuation to line end; add no internal punctuation. - Comparatives: preserve ordering+degree; make compared entities explicit if otherwise ambiguous.

Source Line: 4 Ahi quanto a dir qual era è cosa dura Lexical Inventory: - అయ్యో! - ఎంత - కు - చెప్పు - ఏది - ఉన్నది - అది - వస్తువు - కఠినమైన Assembly Notes: - Interjection placed first; degree adverb modifies the infinitive phrase; infinitive formed by joining “కు” + “చెప్పు” → “చెప్పడానికి”; interrogative “ఏది” precedes past copula “ఉన్నది”; present copula “అది” links to predicate; adjective “కఠినమైన” agrees with noun “వస్తువు”. Target Text: అయ్యో! ఎంత చెప్పడానికి ఏది ఉన్నది అది కఠినమైన వస్తువు
Source Line: 5 esta selva selvaggia e aspra e forte Lexical Inventory: - ఈ - అడవి - అరణ్య - మరియు - కఠినమైన - మరియు - బలమైన Assembly Notes: - Demonstrative “ఈ” before noun; adjectives coordinated by “మరియు” retain original order; all adjectives agree with “అడవి”. Target Text: ఈ అడవి అరణ్య మరియు కఠినమైన మరియు బలమైన
Source Line: 6 che nel pensier rinova la paura! Lexical Inventory: - అది - లో - ఆలోచన - పునరుద్ధరించు - భయం Assembly Notes: - Relative pronoun “అది” introduces clause; preposition “లో” combines with “ఆలోచన” → “ఆలోచనలో”; verb follows locative phrase; object “భయం” follows verb. Target Text: అది ఆలోచనలో పునరుద్ధరించు భయం

### Step 4: Self-Correction via Back-Translation & Grammatical Check For each line: verify Step3 Target Text vs Reference Translation + Step1 Locked Meaning; correct within-line only. Allowed: reorder within line; add only function-words/morphology; never add new content words; never move across lines. Punctuation: keep only end punctuation from source; no internal punctuation. Meaning Drift includes wrong modifier attachment/scope. Output per line bullets with EXACT fields (no extras): Line #, Target Text, Back-Translation, Reference Translation, Checks, Corrected Target Text (if any). Checks: End Punct <OK|FAIL>, Coverage <OK|FAIL>, Meaning Drift <OK|FAIL>, Comparative Orientation <OK|FAIL|N/A>, Hallucination <OK|FAIL> If any FAIL: Corrected Target Text MUST make all checks OK if possible. Comparative Orientation: preserve ordering+degree; treat (A>B) ≡ (B<A) and (A<B) ≡ (B>A); FAIL only if ordering reversed or degree lost. After all lines: if any line still FAILs, output UNVERIFIED with failing Line #s; otherwise do not output UNVERIFIED. Output final Telugu text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- Line 4, Target Text: అయ్యో! అది కఠినమైన వస్తువు ఎంత చెప్పడానికి ఏది ఉన్నది, Back-Translation: “Ah! It is a hard thing how to tell what it was”, Reference Translation: “Ah! how hard a thing it is to tell what … was”, Checks: End Punct OK; Coverage OK; Meaning Drift OK; Comparative Orientation N/A; Hallucination OK, Corrected Target Text: అయ్యో! అది కఠినమైన వస్తువు ఎంత చెప్పడానికి ఏది ఉన్నది
- Line 5, Target Text: ఈ అడవి అరణ్య మరియు కఠినమైన మరియు బలమైన, Back-Translation: “this forest wild and rough and strong”, Reference Translation: “this wild and rough and dense wood”, Checks: End Punct OK; Coverage OK; Meaning Drift OK; Comparative Orientation N/A; Hallucination OK, Corrected Target Text: ఈ అడవి అరణ్య మరియు కఠినమైన మరియు బలమైన
- Line 6, Target Text: అది ఆలోచనలో పునరుద్ధరించు భయం!, Back-Translation: “which in thought renews fear”, Reference Translation: “which in thought renews the fear!”, Checks: End Punct OK; Coverage OK; Meaning Drift OK; Comparative Orientation N/A; Hallucination OK, Corrected Target Text: అది ఆలోచనలో పునరుద్ధరించు భయం!
